{{Formula One|lists}}

[[Formula One]] (F1) is the highest class of [[Open wheel car|open-wheeled]] [[motor racing]] defined by the [[Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile]] (FIA), motorsport's world governing body.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fia.com/en-GB/the-fia/about-fia/Pages/AboutFIA.aspx |title=About FIA |publisher=Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) |access-date=31 October 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110628200958/http://www.fia.com/en-GB/the-fia/about-fia/Pages/AboutFIA.aspx |archive-date=28 June 2011}}</ref> The [[List of Formula One seasons|F1 World Championship season]] consists of a series of races, known as {{not a typo|[[List of Formula One Grands Prix|Grands Prix]]}}, held usually on purpose-built [[List of Formula One circuits|circuits]], and in a few cases on [[Street circuit|closed city streets]].<ref>{{harvnb|Hughes|Tremayne|2002|pp=82–83}}</ref> Each winner is presented with a trophy and the results of each race are combined to determine two annual Championships, one for [[List of Formula One World Drivers' Champions|drivers]] and one for [[List of Formula One World Constructors' Champions|constructors]].<ref>{{cite web|date=7 April 2020|title=2020 Formula One Sporting Regulations|url=https://www.fia.com/sites/default/files/2020_formula_1_sporting_regulations_-_iss_6_-_2020-04-07.pdf|access-date=15 April 2020|publisher=Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA)|pages=3–4, 49–50|format=PDF|archive-date=12 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200412175805/https://www.fia.com/sites/default/files/2020_formula_1_sporting_regulations_-_iss_6_-_2020-04-07.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref> The World Championship for Drivers has been contended since [[1950 Formula One season|1950]],<ref name="history">{{cite web|last1=Williamson|first1=Martin|title=A brief history of Formula One|url=http://en.espn.co.uk/f1/motorsport/story/3831.html|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=4 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180104154609/http://en.espn.co.uk/f1/motorsport/story/3831.html|archive-date=4 January 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> after the Formula One standard was agreed upon in 1946.<ref>{{cite web|title=Timeline of Formula One|url=http://en.espn.co.uk/f1/motorsport/page/2825.html|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=4 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180104154747/http://en.espn.co.uk/f1/motorsport/page/2825.html|archive-date=4 January 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Constructors' Championship was added for the [[1958 Formula One season|1958 season]] and has been awarded ever since.<ref name=history/>
[[File:Prime Minister Keir Starmer meets Sir Lewis Hamilton (54566928382) (cropped).jpg|thumb|300x300px|[[Lewis Hamilton]] has won a record 106 {{not a typo|Grands Prix}} during his career: 21 with [[McLaren]], 84 with [[Mercedes-Benz in Formula One|Mercedes]], and 1 with [[Scuderia Ferrari|Ferrari]].]]
[[Lewis Hamilton]] holds the record for the most race wins in Formula One history, with 106 wins to date. [[Michael Schumacher]], the previous record holder, is second with 91 wins, and [[Max Verstappen]] is third with 73 victories.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Wins By number|url=https://www.statsf1.com/en/statistiques/pilote/victoire/nombre.aspx|access-date=11 October 2026|publisher=Stats F1|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100318043059/https://www.statsf1.com/en/statistiques/pilote/victoire/nombre.aspx|archive-date=18 March 2010|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Race Wins|url=https://www.chicanef1.com/records.pl?pos=1&who=d&t=C&per=&con=&until=&nc=0&hideindy=0|access-date=26 October 2020|publisher=Chicane F1|archive-date=29 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201029154758/https://www.chicanef1.com/records.pl?pos=1&who=d&t=C&per=&con=&until=&nc=0&hideindy=0|url-status=live}}</ref> Hamilton also holds the distinction of having the longest time between his first win and his last. He won his first Grand Prix at the {{F1GP||2007 Canadian}}, and his last at the {{F1GP||2026 Barcelona-Catalunya}}, a span of 19&nbsp;years and 4&nbsp;days.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.statsf1.com/en/statistiques/pilote/victoire/interval.aspx |title=Interval between the first and last |publisher=StatsF1 |access-date=14 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240711150554/https://www.statsf1.com/en/statistiques/pilote/victoire/interval.aspx |archive-date=11 July 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Riccardo Patrese]] holds the record for the longest period of time between two race wins – more than six-and-a-half years between the {{F1GP||1983 South African}} and the {{F1GP||1990 San Marino}}.<ref>{{cite web|title=Wins: Interval between two|url=http://www.statsf1.com/en/statistiques/pilote/victoire/ecart.aspx|access-date=3 January 2018|publisher=StatsF1|archive-date=7 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181007101802/http://www.statsf1.com/en/statistiques/pilote/victoire/ecart.aspx|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Mario Andretti]] had to wait the longest time between his maiden victory at the {{F1GP||1971 South African}} and his second win – coming five years, seven months and 18 days later at the {{F1GP||1976 Japanese}}.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Leslie|first1=Jack|date=18 August 2017|title=The 5 Drivers with the Biggest Gap between First and Second F1 Wins|url=https://wtf1.com/post/the-5-drivers-with-the-biggest-gaps-between-first-and-second-f1-wins/|access-date=3 January 2018|publisher=WTF1|archive-date=4 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180104073607/https://wtf1.com/post/the-5-drivers-with-the-biggest-gaps-between-first-and-second-f1-wins/|url-status=live}}</ref> Verstappen holds the record for the most consecutive wins, having won ten {{not a typo|Grands Prix}} in a row from the [[2023 Miami Grand Prix]] to the [[2023 Italian Grand Prix]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Saunders |first=Nate |date=3 September 2023 |title=Max Verstappen claims record 10th straight F1 win at Italian Grand Prix |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/f1/story/_/id/38319156/max-verstappen-claims-record-10th-straight-f1-win-italian-grand-prix |access-date=25 February 2025 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260704124959/https://www.espn.co.uk/f1/story/_/id/38319156/max-verstappen-claims-record-10th-straight-f1-win-italian-grand-prix |archive-date=4 July 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Verstappen is also the youngest winner of a Grand Prix; he was 18 years and 228 days old when he won the {{F1GP||2016 Spanish}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Youngest driver to win a Formula One World Championship race|url=https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/youngest-driver-to-win-a-formula-one-world-championship-race|access-date=8 August 2020|publisher=Guinness World Records|archive-date=12 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200812205013/https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/youngest-driver-to-win-a-formula-one-world-championship-race|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Luigi Fagioli]] is the oldest winner of a Formula One Grand Prix; he was 53&nbsp;years and 22&nbsp;days old when he won the {{F1GP||1951 French}}.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://en.espnf1.com/f1/motorsport/story/68880.html|title=Over forty but still fast|publisher=ESPN|date=3 February 2012|access-date=18 June 2012|first=Steven|last=Lynch|archive-date=25 April 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140425072401/http://en.espnf1.com/f1/motorsport/story/68880.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

As of the {{F1GP||2026 Singapore}}, out of the 782 drivers who started a Grand Prix,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.statsf1.com/en/statistiques/pilote/gp/chronologie.aspx|title=Grands Prix chronology|publisher=Stats F1|access-date=11 October 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141021070356/http://www.statsf1.com/en/statistiques/pilote/gp/chronologie.aspx|archive-date=21 October 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> there have been 116 Formula One Grand Prix winners.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |url=http://www.statsf1.com/en/statistiques/pilote/victoire/chronologie.aspx |title=Wins chronology |publisher=Stats F1 |access-date=11 October 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201105132531/https://www.statsf1.com/en/statistiques/pilote/victoire/chronologie.aspx |archive-date=5 November 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref> The first Grand Prix winner was [[Giuseppe Farina]] at the {{F1GP||1950 British}}, and the most recent driver to score their first Grand Prix win is [[Kimi Antonelli]] who took his first win at the {{F1GP||2026 Chinese}}.<ref name=":0" /> Three {{not a typo|Grands Prix}}, the [[1951 French Grand Prix|1951 French]], the [[1956 Argentine Grand Prix|1956 Argentine]] and the [[1957 British Grand Prix|1957 British]] {{not a typo|Grands Prix}}, were won by two drivers sharing a car, so both drivers in each event were credited with a Grand Prix victory.<ref>{{Cite web|title=111 F1 winners|url=https://www.andrewnoakes.com/blog/f1-winners.html|access-date=26 October 2020|publisher=Andrew Noakes|archive-date=16 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211116153357/https://www.andrewnoakes.com/blog/f1-winners.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In addition to event-specific trophies, [[gold medal]]s have been awarded to all victors from the [[2022 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix]] onwards.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/sports/f1-drivers-to-get-medals-for-race-wins-idUSKBN2SA08M/ |title=F1 drivers to get medals for race wins |last=Baldwin |first=Alan |date=20 November 2022 |work=[[Reuters]] |publisher=[[Thomson Reuters]] |access-date=29 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250629161802/https://www.reuters.com/article/sports/f1-drivers-to-get-medals-for-race-wins-idUSKBN2SA08M/ |archive-date=29 June 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

This list includes the winners of the 11 [[Indianapolis 500]] races between [[1950 Indianapolis 500|1950]] and [[1960 Indianapolis 500|1960]], as they were part of the World Championships in early years, even though they were not run by Formula One regulations, nor are they referred to as {{not a typo|Grands Prix}}.<ref>{{harvnb|Smith|2019|pp=10, 76}}</ref>

[[File:Schumacher (Ferrari) in practice at USGP 2005.jpg|thumb|right|[[Michael Schumacher]] held the record until [[2020 Portuguese Grand Prix|2020]], with 91 victories.]]
[[File:2024-08-25 Motorsport, Formel 1, Großer Preis der Niederlande 2024 STP 3857 by Stepro.jpg|thumb|right|[[Max Verstappen]] has won 73 Grands Prix, and is the youngest winner in Formula One history.]]
[[File:Sebastian Vettel 2013 Catalonia test (19-22 Feb) Day 2.jpg|thumb|right|[[Sebastian Vettel]] took 53 victories across 16 seasons.]]
[[File:Alain Prost - Williams FW15C during practice for the 1993 British Grand Prix (33557468541).jpg|thumb|right|[[Alain Prost]] held the record until [[2001 Belgian Grand Prix|2001]], with 51 victories.]]
[[File:2026 Chinese GP - Mercedes - Kimi Antonelli - Qualifying.jpg|thumb|[[Kimi Antonelli]] is the 116th and latest first-time Grand Prix winner, taking his maiden victory at the [[2026 Chinese Grand Prix]].]]
